affiliations.role_title: Graduate student pursuing a Ph.D. in geography
affiliations.research_notes: CIA and scholarly accounts identify Robinson as a geography/cartography graduate student recruited in 1941. Ohio State is an institution attended, not an employer.
The scholarly recruitment history calls Ackerman a Harvard instructor when Hartshorne hired him; the American Heritage Center independently dates his Harvard faculty service to 1940-1948.

affiliations.organization_name_as_found: Board of Governors, Federal Reserve System
affiliations.research_notes: The Truman Library chronology places Federal Reserve Board service in 1939-1941 and OSS/Joint Chiefs analytical service beginning in 1941, with no intervening affiliation identified.
Kaysen's first-person account says he finished his current National Bureau assignment before going to Washington in about May 1942.
Kaysen directly described himself as a Columbia graduate student in early 1942. Columbia is not classified as his employer.
Mason's first-person chronology identifies this consulting assignment immediately before his permanent 1941 move to Washington for OSS.
The oral-history interviewer notes Mason was a Harvard full professor by 1937. No formal end date for this appointment is asserted.

affiliations.role_title: Co-director of studies for the Temporary National Economic Committee
affiliations.research_notes: Mason identified this as his first government assignment; the reviewed transcript did not supply exact dates.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Captain Arthur H. Robinson is the geographer recruited in 1941 who led the COI/OSS map unit.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact name and initial, captain rank, Box 651 index entry, institutional chronology, and documented map leadership align.
claims.temporal_assessment: CIA and university accounts place his recruitment and cartographic work from 1941.
claims.match_notes: The multi-source role chronology is highly specific; the physical personnel file remains unreviewed.

claims.claim_text: Immediately before his 1941 recruitment, Arthur H. Robinson was a geography/cartography graduate student at Ohio State University.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The CIA Museum calls Robinson a graduate student pursuing a geography doctorate when the COI cartography section hired him.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on exact name, discipline, date, OSS role, and index rank.
claims.match_notes: This is student status. No reviewed source establishes Ohio State as his employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Edward A. Ackerman is the Harvard geographer recruited into the COI/OSS geographic research organization.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact name and middle initial, NARA index entry, Harvard chronology, specialty, and specific recruitment history align.
claims.temporal_assessment: Harvard service beginning in 1940 and COI recruitment in 1941 form a coherent wartime chronology.
claims.match_notes: The physical Box 2 personnel file remains the best route to exact appointment paperwork.

claims.claim_text: Edward A. Ackerman was a Harvard geography instructor immediately before his recruitment into the COI/OSS organization.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The recruitment history identifies Ackerman as a Harvard instructor; the American Heritage Center independently dates his Harvard faculty service to 1940-1948.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on exact identity, discipline, employer, and specific recruitment sequence.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate transition, with Harvard service continuing beyond the initial wartime recruitment date.
claims.match_notes: The continuing faculty date is preserved and not silently truncated at OSS entry.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Emile Despres is the economist whose official chronology records OSS and Joint Chiefs analytical service from 1941 to 1944.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact distinctive name, Box 183 index entry, occupation, and official 1941-1944 wartime-service chronology align.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official chronology directly brackets Federal Reserve work and OSS service.
claims.match_notes: The Truman Library finding aid is specific to Despres's papers and wartime appointments.

claims.claim_text: Emile Despres's last documented civilian employer before OSS service was the Federal Reserve Board, where he advised the chairman.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Truman Library dates his Federal Reserve Board role to 1939-1941 and his OSS/Joint Chiefs analytical work to 1941-1944.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by a person-specific official archival chronology and the exact NARA index name.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded with no intervening affiliation identified.
claims.match_notes: The claim is limited to the sequence established by the official finding aid.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Carl Kaysen is the economist who entered OSS in 1942 and later received an Army Air Forces commission.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact distinctive name, Box 394 index entry, MIT biography, and detailed first-person OSS and military chronology align.
claims.temporal_assessment: The first-person account places his OSS move in about May 1942 and subsequent Army Air Forces intelligence service.
claims.match_notes: The physical personnel file remains unreviewed, so the entity status remains high confidence rather than confirmed.

claims.claim_text: Carl Kaysen's last civilian employer before OSS was the National Bureau of Economic Research, where he was a part-time research assistant.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Kaysen said he completed his National Bureau assignment before going to Washington for OSS in about May 1942.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on a detailed first-person transition account and corroborating institutional biography.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate transition in about May 1942.
claims.match_notes: The source does not establish the start date, which remains blank.

claims.claim_text: Carl Kaysen was also a Columbia graduate student immediately before his 1942 move to OSS.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: In his first-person account, Kaysen described concurrent Columbia graduate study and part-time National Bureau research before recruitment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the same detailed first-person chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate student affiliation in early 1942.
claims.match_notes: Columbia is classified as an institution attended, not an employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Edward S. Mason is the Harvard economist who said William Langer recruited him into OSS in 1941.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact name and initial, Box 490 index entry, Harvard role, 1941 recruitment, and senior OSS economic position align.
claims.temporal_assessment: Mason's official oral history directly recounts his 1941 OSS recruitment and earlier assignments.
claims.match_notes: The source-row grade PD is preserved without speculative expansion.

claims.claim_text: Edward S. Mason's immediate pre-OSS government assignment was consulting for the Office of Production Management on raw-material problems.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Mason placed this consulting work just before his permanent 1941 move to Washington for OSS.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by Mason's first-person archival interview and exact index identity.
claims.match_notes: The relationship is classified as a government assignment, not a civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: Edward S. Mason's last documented civilian employer before his permanent OSS move was Harvard University, where he was a professor of economics.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The interview establishes a Harvard full professorship by 1937 and a permanent Washington move for OSS in 1941.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by a first-person archival interview and exact index identity.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded; the project does not claim that Harvard formally ended the appointment in 1941.
claims.match_notes: The claim separates civilian employment from the intervening production-management consulting assignment.

claims.claim_text: Before OSS, Edward S. Mason also co-directed Labor Department studies for the Temporary National Economic Committee.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Mason called the Labor Department research his first government assignment but did not give exact dates in the reviewed passage.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by Mason's first-person archival interview.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar; not presented as the immediate predecessor to OSS.
claims.match_notes: The earlier assignment remains separate from both Harvard employment and the later Office of Production Management consultancy.
